The Battle of Bunker Hill was a battle o.why: Stated in the first sentence of Wikipedia's article ('during the siege of Boston in the first stage of the American Revolutionary War') and everywhere the battle is mentioned; the battle and the war co-occur about 17,000 times. It can also be worked out from the battle's date (June 1775) and its place in the siege of Boston, so it is rated unlikely rather than very unlikely to be derived.

notes: Mirrors history-replace-0014: deletes the original fact. The inheritance queries are rephrased around the original class: the eighteenth-century query keeps the inheritance derivation; the Madison query has no counterpart for the Revolutionary War (there was no president, and Washington took command of the Continental Army only after Lexington and Concord), so it is replaced by a same-war comparison with Saratoga. Both worlds list the battle's date and its place in the siege of Boston as going with the deleted fact, since either would re-derive the war; in w2 the Warren-Bunker Hill link goes too (the history-delete-0002 pattern). Risk: a model may still re-derive the war from the battle's opponents (colonial militia against British regulars), though those fit the War of 1812 as well, so they do not settle it.
